A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with LoGra-Med renamed ExGra-Med. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original pre-training comparisons, MedVQA results, component ablations, chatbot evaluations and zero-shot classification experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and adds controls, sensitivity and representation analyses, and clinician assessments of generated captions.

M1.justification: The triplet graphs, message passing, barycenter alignment, Hamming loss, IMLE gradient estimation, joint autoregressive training and optional DCI remain. Renaming, additional implementation explanations and experimental component substitutions do not establish a revised default algorithm.

E1.justification: The PMC pre-training data, three MedVQA datasets, chatbot dataset and 23 zero-shot datasets are retained. V3 adds a focused expert assessment task for caption coverage and medical correctness across the existing imaging modalities, without expanding downstream benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: V3 Tables 1–2 add GeoCLAP, PAC-S and IMAGEBIND to the 10% and 40% pre-training comparisons, substantially expanding comparison with methods aligning multiple modalities. Existing comparators remain. The LVM-Med comparison discussed in Appendix E reuses the earlier two-graph ablation results.

E3.justification: V3 introduces extended-caption LLaVA-Med controls and describes additional Stage-2 training time. New protocols include five physicians each rating 200 modality-specific samples on two five-point scales, and representation analysis using 1,000 unseen image-text pairs. New ablation configurations are also specified; existing benchmark splits and training epoch counts are retained.

E4.justification: V3 adds tests of caption augmentation alone, alternative caption generators, loss weights, removing original captions, replacing the barycenter, and neighbor-count sensitivity. It also adds feature-separation analysis and expert caption-quality assessment. Existing ablations are retained across renaming and relocation; Table 17 redisplays earlier benchmark values rather than establishing another independent experiment.

E5.justification: Appendix J.2 and Figure 6 introduce descriptive dispersion reporting through feature-similarity medians, interquartile ranges, whiskers and outliers. Caption-rating distributions are also added. Neither version reports repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial baseline, control, ablation and clinician-rating results. Existing reported values also change: the 40% SLAKE average rises from 84.99 to 85.15 in Table 2, and DCI overall performance changes from 74.9 to 75.1 in v1 Table 3 versus v3 Table 5. V3 Tables 6 and 17 still retain 84.99, leaving an inconsistency. Chatbot and zero-shot results are retained.

T1.justification: The metric and geodesic theorems, Proposition 1, Lemma 1 and their appendix proofs are retained. SGA replaces SoGA in notation, and the numbered structured-graph definition restates material previously in Section 3.6; these are presentation changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: diagnosing autoregressive data dependence, introducing efficient triplet graph alignment, establishing graph-distance properties, and achieving data-efficient medical vision-language performance. The additional evidence does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: V3 newly interprets the benefit of captions alone versus graph alignment, justifies average pooling despite overlapping similarity distributions, and argues that caption noise should have limited downstream effects because extended captions only guide pre-training alignment. These substantially expand the mechanism discussion. The noise-impact argument remains untested directly; the earlier architecture-related limitations are largely restated.

D1.justification: V3 adds a repository link, specifies open-question recall and closed-question accuracy, documents loss-weight and neighbor-count settings, and supplies annotation interfaces and rating guidelines. Reported Stage-1 training time changes from seven to 6.5 hours. Core architecture, optimizer, learning rates, hardware, dataset splits and caption-generation prompt remain documented as before.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds positioning against PAC-S, GeoCLAP and IMAGEBIND. New Appendix E substantially develops the relationship to fused Gromov-Wasserstein transport and LVM-Med, comparing computational requirements, solvers, graph construction and theoretical contributions. This extends research positioning beyond citation-format changes.

P1.justification: V3 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction and experimental narrative, renames the method, and reorganizes the document. Detailed graph definitions, chatbot evaluation, zero-shot evaluation and limitations move into reorganized appendices, alongside new dedicated discussion and analysis sections.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with parameter-scaled markers and an expanded caption. V3 adds control and ablation tables, a similarity boxplot, annotation-interface screenshots and caption-rating histograms. Existing figures and tables are relocated or reformatted, including substantial changes to table arrangement, captions and theorem presentation.

improvement.justification: V1 lacked a direct control testing whether enriched captions alone explain the gains. V3 Table 3 addresses this, reporting 69.41 for caption-augmented LLaVA-Med versus 72.52 for ExGra-Med at 10% pre-training. Together with closer multi-modal baselines, targeted structural ablations and expert caption review, this substantially strengthens method validation. The remaining SLAKE inconsistency and absent repeated-run uncertainty limit precision, but the new controls provide a clear overall quality gain.
